observation_sampling.method: uniform without replacement over cached person-mask depth points

mesh_sampling.triangle_distribution: uniform by face index without replacement

nearest_operation: torch.cdist from sampled observations to sampled mesh points, followed by amin over sampled mesh points
seed_contract: stable_seed(protocol seed, observation id, epoch); both observation and mesh samples therefore change across epochs
differentiability: Piecewise differentiable through selected barycentric samples into vertices and upstream heads. Sampling indices and nearest-sample argmin are discrete.
material_findings: The training loss has a nonzero Monte Carlo floor even for perfect coplanar geometry.
On the controlled unequal-area mesh, increasing 4096 to 16384 samples reduced the mean perfect-geometry floor from 1.59 mm-equivalent to 0.33 mm-equivalent.
For a fixed +30 mm perturbation, adjacent-seed full-vertex gradient cosine rose from about 0.36 at 4096 samples to about 0.70 at 16384 samples.
Area weighting slightly reduced the floor at 4096/8192 but did not materially improve perturbed-gradient cosine in this test.
recommendation: Before another SAM training run, freeze sampling for controlled comparisons and evaluate a higher sample count. Do not replace with area weighting solely from this toy result; validate on MHR DEV geometry first.
